svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: ehr-rwe-eln data: OMOP in the lake, one Aurora schema per module
svg.desc: The OMOP CDM v5.4 tables are Iceberg tables in the cdm namespace of an S3 table bucket, read through Redshift Serverless: clinical events keyed to person, derived eras and cohorts, and the Athena vocabularies keyed to concept. Aurora PostgreSQL holds each module's results in the dq, tte, eln, synth, and curation schemas, and the app's own state. Genotypes, registries, the FHIR bundle, and data cards are files under data/.
svg.text: Row counts are from the 23,421-person build. Open the SVG on its own and hover a table for what it holds.

g.title: scripts/build_omop.py builds cdm in the staging Postgres and scripts/publish_omop.py copies it to the lake. Alembic migrations create the Aurora schemas and record their version in public.alembic_version. Foreign keys on the left are OMOP's own; Iceberg does not enforce them. A second patient population would be a second CDM namespace, not a second database.
g.text: OMOP in the lake, module results in Aurora

g.title: The OHDSI standard tables, as Apache Iceberg, read through Redshift Serverless. In OMOP's model, 17 foreign keys point at person and 118 at concept.
g.text: Lake: cdm, OMOP CDM v5.4 in S3 Tables

svg.text: Clinical data: every row has person_id, a foreign key to person

a.title: One row per patient: birth year, sex, race, ethnicity.
The span of time each person's records cover. Analyses count events only inside it.
Date and cause for people who died during the simulation.
Encounters: outpatient, inpatient, emergency, and others.
Diagnoses, coded in SNOMED.
Prescriptions and administrations, coded in RxNorm and CVX.
Procedures, coded in SNOMED.
Lab results and vital signs, coded in LOINC. The ELN bridge adds its lab results here.
Facts that are not measurements: history, social, survey.
Devices used on or implanted in a person.
Samples from lab notebook entries, written by the ELN bridge.
Links each ELN specimen to the measurements taken from it. Written by the ELN bridge.

svg.text: Derived: built from the clinical tables

a.title: Spans of continuous diagnosis, built by the cohort pipeline.
Spans of continuous drug use, built by the cohort pipeline.
People and index dates for each cohort definition in YAML.
Source name, ETL date, and vocabulary version.

svg.text: Vocabularies from Athena: every *_concept_id is a foreign key to concept

a.title: Every code from every vocabulary, with its standard concept. A diagnosis or drug in the clinical tables is a concept_id here.
Mappings between concepts, such as a source code to its standard concept.
Every concept's ancestors, so a cohort can ask for a drug class instead of each drug.
Alternative names for concepts.
SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, ICD10CM, and the small ones.
Which table a concept belongs in: Condition, Drug, Measurement.
Kinds of concept within a vocabulary.
Ingredient amounts per drug, for dose calculations.

svg.text: Also defined, empty in this build: provider, care_site, location, cost, payer_plan_period, note, note_nlp,
visit_detail, episode, episode_event, dose_era, metadata, source_to_concept_map, cohort_definition, relationship (724 rows).

g.title: Each module's results and the app's state, in Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL, created by Alembic migrations. Arrows are foreign keys.

a.title: When a run happened and its overall scores.
One row per DQD check: threshold, violations, pass.
When the trial protocols ran, and on how many people.
The bias report: attrition, balance, estimates.
The free-text lab notebook entries.
What Claude extracted, as validated JSON.
Method, privacy budget, seed, and provenance.
The released rows, as JSON per row.
Links each notebook subject code to a person in cdm.person. Kept as data, not a foreign key, the way a lab keeps its subject registry apart from its notebooks.
Fidelity, utility, trial parity, and privacy risk reports per release.
Which variants were curated, every source and version used, and for eval runs the agreement with ClinVar expert panels.
Evidence, criteria met and not assessed with reasons, points, and class.
Literature evidence Claude proposed, with its PMID and quote, verified or rejected with the reason. Changes nothing until a curator accepts it.
A curator's decision: who, when, the proposals accepted, the criteria, points, and the class chosen, with a note when it differs from the score.
Where each carrier's HPO phenotype score falls among the study's subjects. Context for the curator, not evidence. No foreign key: matched by variant_id.
Where Exomiser's phenotype score ranks the variant's gene for each carrier. Context for the curator, not evidence. No foreign key: matched by variant_id.

svg.text: synth, continued, and the app's own

a.title: Each scheduled privacy check: which releases it reran and what changed. The monitor task writes one a day.
Each release's recipients, its withdrawal, and their confirmations that they deleted it.
Person counts per concept, precomputed from the lake by scripts/build_omop_stats.py, so the agent's public calls never reach Redshift. Counts under 11 are suppressed and never stored.
Tokens /api/agent spent each day, for the daily limit. The langgraph schema, not drawn, holds the literature graph's checkpoints.

g.title: The staging Postgres and files under data/, which is gitignored.

a.title: The ETL, cohorts, and the ELN bridge write OMOP to ehr_rwe_eln here, and publish_omop.py copies it to the lake. pytest writes to ehr_rwe_eln_test and rolls back; it holds no patients.
The simulated genotype study, laid out as dbGaP distributes one. GWAS tools read files, not tables.
Links the genomics and ELN study codes to OMOP persons, kept apart from the study files.
The generated entries with their answers, and the FHIR R4 Specimen and Observation export.
What each synthetic release is, how it was made, and what it is safe to use for.

g.title: Aurora table: module results, app state
